function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here’s a quick guide on where you can order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just want it delivered right to your door.

| Option | What it offers | How to find it | Tips |
|--------|----------------|----------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Freshly baked cakes, often customizable | Google “cake shop near me” or use Yelp / Google Maps | Look for bakeries with good reviews and photos of their cakes. Many offer pickup or local delivery. |
| **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety from local artisans to national brands | Order via websites like **Etsy**, **Amazon Handmade**, or **Zazzle** | Great for unique designs or custom messages. Check shipping times and packaging. |
| **Food‑delivery apps** | Same‑day delivery from restaurants & bakeries | Use **Uber Eats**, **DoorDash**, **Grubhub**, **Postmates**, or **SkipTheDishes** | Search “cakes” or “desserts.” Delivery fees vary; some apps have free delivery promotions. |
| **Grocery delivery** | Cakes from supermarkets or specialty aisles | Order through **Instacart**, **Shipt**, **Amazon Fresh**, or the grocery’s own app (e.g., Walmart Grocery, Kroger, Safeway) | Ideal if you need other groceries at the same time. Delivery windows may be longer than food‑delivery apps. |
| **Specialty cake shops** | Custom wedding cakes, themed cakes, premium ingredients | Find them via Google or Instagram (search hashtags like #customcakes + your city). | Contact them directly for quotes and design ideas. Some accept online orders, others prefer phone/email. |
| **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (often novelty or seasonal) | Look at sites like **Goldbelly**, **Cake Delivery Box**, or local subscription services | Fun for gifts or trying new flavors. Check the subscription terms and cancellation policy. |

### Quick Steps to Order

1. **Decide on the type of cake** – birthday, wedding, custom design, or just a simple store‑bought one.
2. **Choose a platform** – local bakery for freshness, delivery app for convenience, or subscription box for novelty.
3. **Check reviews & photos** – ensures quality and helps you pick the right style.
4. **Place your order** – most platforms let you specify size, flavor, frosting, decorations, and delivery time.
5. **Confirm details** – double‑check address, delivery window, and any special instructions (e.g., “no plastic wrap”).

If you tell me your city or zip code, I can look up specific bakeries or delivery options in your area. Happy cake hunting!
